claims.text: TRP-04005 was sold and settled as an upfront-quoted trip: the fare breakdown carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 22.25 and distance_charged_km 14.20, and the trip record's booking events fix the quote basis at 14.20 km and 25 minutes. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges on such a trip were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run at all and no fare recomputation is available. The 6.37 km by which the trace exceeds the quote is therefore incapable of being converted into a refund, a recomputed fare, or any rider-side liability - the extra distance is a cost the policy places on the driver on an upfront trip, not a charge the rider can be made to bear.

The rider paid exactly what was quoted and not a cent more: charged_total is 22.25 and quoted_fare_sgd is 22.25, so the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote - the only sum POL-RD-11(a) makes refundable - is 0.00. The fare breakdown shows no ERP lines, no tolls, an airport_surcharge line of 0.00 and a waiting_time_fee of 0.00, so there is no pass-through or statutory line under POL-RD-09 on which any further amount, still less the driver's SGD 6.00, could be built. The present payment state (CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is the complete and correct settlement of this trip, and the driver's claim should be dismissed with that state unchanged.

POL-RD-11 forecloses the very route the driver's claim takes. Its rule states in terms that the driver's unrecovered cost on a detour 'is not recoverable from the rider under this clause', and the SGD 6.00 sought in this dispute is precisely that unrecovered cost. The driver is the filing party; it is for him to point to a clause of the policy in force that shifts his detour cost onto a rider who has already paid the fixed fare in full, and no clause of the route-deviation policy does so. A claim that asks the tribunal to do what the governing clause expressly forbids cannot be granted.

The rider does not dispute that she asked for the stop, and the record fully corroborates her: at 15:59:50 the rider's in-app message asks to stop at Northpoint first, and the platform-resolved waypoint_hint carried on that message sits 55.0 m from the trace's nearest fix - well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test. That concession costs the rider nothing. POL-RD-11 routes a rider-requested detour to POL-RD-04, whose compensation is a policy-rate driver payment, and POL-GEN-03 defines driver_compensation_sgd as a platform-funded or fee-funded payment to the driver - not a charge payable by the rider. Whichever way the causation question is read, the rider's payment state does not change, and no refund or compensation may be levied out of the fixed fare the rider has already paid.

The sum claimed is not produced by any clause's arithmetic. The rider's exposure over the quote is 0.00, and the only distance-based payment the policy provides on these facts is POL-RD-04's rate of SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, capped at SGD 15.00, which on this record's own figures - 20.57 km traced against 14.20 km billed - yields 4.78 rounded up to SGD 4.80. A round figure of SGD 6.00 corresponds to no line of the fare breakdown and to no formula in the policy, and to the extent any such payment were made it is, under POL-GEN-03, a platform-funded or fee-funded payment to the driver rather than a rider charge. The claim as filed cannot be granted in the form pleaded.

The driver's filing identifies no artifact and names no clause: the claim text asserts a detour and demands SGD 6.00, without citing a single evidence ID. POL-RD-08 requires a party invoking an exculpatory or compensatory clause to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and provides that an assertion which cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. The driver is the party asserting that money is owed and so carries the burden of proving the facts that make it owed; an uncited assertion does not discharge that burden, and the artifacts in the bundle that do speak to the request are the rider's own message and the trace, not the driver's pleading.

claims.text: The chat log carries a rider instruction to make the Northpoint stop: MSG-04005-003, sent by RIDER R-1846 at 2026-09-27T15:59:50, reads 'uncle later can stop at Northpoint first? need to collect my cake, 5 min only then go AMK', and the platform resolved its waypoint_hint at ingest to 1.4289, 103.8357 labelled 'Northpoint City'. The driver accepted four seconds later ('ok can', MSG-04005-004). POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are therefore met: the instruction comes from the rider, not the driver, and it identifies a place specifically enough to act on rather than something vague like 'go the fast way'.

POL-RD-04(b) and the corroboration limb are met on timestamps and coordinates. The instruction was sent at 15:59:50, before the trip started at 16:00:20 and before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, so it is inside the three-minute allowance. The gps_trace corroborates it exactly as the clause requires: the nearest fix to the resolved waypoint_hint (fix index 97, 16:16:26) is 55.0 m away, far inside the 200 m threshold that POL-RD-04 sets, and the derived waypoint_approach block marks within_threshold true.

The rider's own counterparty_statement concedes the request in terms: 'Yes I asked him to stop at Northpoint'. Her only objection is to paying more, not to whether she asked, so the factual foundation of the driver's case - a rider-requested detour actually driven - is common ground on the file and not something the driver has to prove against her.

The deviation the driver complains of is real and measured, not asserted. The governing trace figure under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km 20.57 km against a booked optimal of 14.2 km, an excess of 6.37 km or 44.86%, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). The record shows one off-corridor waypoint, corroborated to within 55 m, and no other instruction in the chat log, so under POL-RD-04 the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied and is not chargeable against the driver.

Separately from the exoneration, and on the face of the ledger, POL-RD-04's compensation limb is satisfied: fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 14.20 while the gps_trace records 20.57 km, so the rider was billed for 6.37 km less than was driven - a shortfall well above the 1.0 km trigger. At the policy's SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre the compensation is 6.37 x 0.75 = SGD 4.7775, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 4.80, and that is inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap.

The rider's answer - 'the price was fixed when I booked' - does not defeat this claim, and the driver does not fight it. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted 22.25, charged_total 22.25, no ERP lines, no surcharge, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so under POL-RD-11 there is no distance-or-time refund for the rider however large the excess; POL-RD-11 expressly says the driver's unrecovered cost on a rider-requested detour is compensated under POL-RD-04 instead. The rider loses nothing and the driver is paid on the clause the policy names.

The policy arithmetic, not the driver's ask, fixes the figure, and the driver accepts it. He filed for SGD 6.00; POL-RD-04 yields SGD 4.80 on 6.37 unbilled kilometres. Under POL-GEN-03 a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling carries amount_sgd at the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd, which is the outcome this record licenses on the merits.

Every artifact this claim rests on is clean, so no escalation or discount is in play. EV-CHAT-04005, EV-TRIP-04005, EV-FARE-04005 and EV-GPS-04005 are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, and the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 195 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, largest interval 10 s, largest straight-line step 216.7 m and highest implied speed 78.0 km/h - nowhere near the 90 s gap, 500 m jump or 30 s cadence limbs. Confidence is therefore not capped below the 0.70 floor under POL-GEN-02(2) and POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered.

The driver-profile check that POL-RD-06 requires comes back clean and should be recorded as such. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 330, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established: no balance is resolved against the driver, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available on this trip and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The excess is in any event not MATERIAL - 6.37 km is under the 8.0 km limb and 44.86% is under the 50% limb.

For completeness and disclosure: no traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-04005-01 is MISSING - admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, payload null - and I name that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. The driver asserts no external traffic cause at all, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked, that absence is not an exculpatory clause invoked against any cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it; the driver's case stands on the chat log and the trace, not on an empty advisory slot.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This is an upfront-quoted RYDE_X trip (TRP-04005): Rider R-1846 booked Causeway Point to Ang Mo Kio Hub for a fixed fare of SGD 22.25 (EV-FARE-04005 quoted_fare_sgd 22.25; distance_charged_km 14.20; EV-TRIP-04005 booked optimal 14.20 km, 25 min). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-04005) records 20.57 km driven, an excess of 6.37 km or 44.86% over the booked route, which establishes a route deviation under POL-RD-01.

The deviation is the rider's own request. MSG-04005-003 (EV-CHAT-04005), sent by the rider at 15:59:50, asks the driver to stop at Northpoint first to collect a cake; the platform resolved that message's waypoint_hint to Northpoint City (1.4289, 103.8357), and the trace's nearest fix passes 55.0 m away, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test. The rider does not dispute the request in her statement. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes the detour excess from any deviation charge against the driver.

Because the fare was fixed at booking, POL-RD-11 governs the rider's side: she is already whole on distance and time, POL-RD-02 does not run, and she owes nothing further. charged_total is 22.25, equal to the quote, so charged_over_quote is 0.00; there are no ERP, toll, airport-surcharge or waiting-time lines. The rider's payment state stands unchanged, and the driver's request for SGD 6.00 is not charged to her.

What remains is the driver's compensation under POL-RD-04. He was billed for 14.20 km but drove 20.57 km, a shortfall of 6.37 km, above the 1.0 km trigger. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 6.37 x 0.75 = SGD 4.7775, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 4.80, within the SGD 15.00 cap. The SGD 6.00 originally claimed corresponds to no line of the fare breakdown and to no formula in the policy. Under POL-GEN-03 this is platform/fee-funded driver compensation (driver_compensation_sgd), not a charge on the rider, and on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure. The monetary effect (SGD 4.80) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes on issue.

No escalation applies. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (195 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, largest step 216.7 m, highest speed 78.0 km/h). Trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown. No exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact: EV-ADVIS-04005-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0, but the driver asserts no external traffic cause and POL-RD-03 is not invoked, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor.

On the POL-RD-06 check: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 330 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral arises; the deviation is also not material (6.37 km is under 8.0 km and 44.86% is under 50%), and no billing-integrity referral arises because there is no unmatched charge line. The rider's point that the driver's filing narrative cites no evidence ID is noted but does not change the outcome: the driver's brief and the rider's own artifacts establish the facts, and no finding rests on the narrative alone.

To both parties. This was an upfront-quoted trip: the fare was fixed at booking at SGD 22.25, and the rider was charged exactly SGD 22.25 (charged over quote = SGD 0.00). On an upfront trip POL-RD-11 closes the distance and time lines to any refund, so no refund to the rider arises on those lines, and no pass-through or statutory line applies here (no ERP, no tolls, airport surcharge SGD 0.00, waiting-time fee SGD 0.00).

The trace records 20.57 km driven against a booked optimal of 14.20 km - an excess of 6.37 km (44.9%). That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so a deviation is established; it is not material (6.37 km is under the 8.0 km limb and 44.9% is under the 50% limb).

The deviation is fully attributable to the rider's own request. The in-app chat (MSG-04005-003, sent 2026-09-27 15:59:50, before the vehicle left the optimal corridor) reads 'uncle later can stop at Northpoint first? need to collect my cake, 5 min only then go AMK', and the platform-resolved waypoint on that message sits 55 m from the trace's nearest fix (fix 97) - far inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test. The rider's own statement confirms the request ('Yes I asked him to stop at Northpoint'). Under POL-RD-04 the detour is exonerated and no adverse finding sits against the driver.

Because the trip is upfront-priced, POL-RD-11 directs the driver's rider-requested detour cost to POL-RD-04 rather than to the rider. POL-RD-04's compensation limb applies: the rider was billed for 14.20 km while the trace records 20.57 km, a shortfall of 6.37 km, well over the 1.0 km trigger. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 6.37 x 0.75 = SGD 4.7775, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 4.80, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The driver asked for SGD 6.00; no line of the fare breakdown and no formula in the policy produces SGD 6.00, so the figure is the policy's SGD 4.80, not the sum pleaded. Under POL-GEN-03 a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling carries the same figure in amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd; the payment is platform-funded, so the rider's settled fare does not change.

On the remaining points: the rider's argument that the driver's original filing text cites no evidence ID (POL-RD-08) is noted, but the driver's case now identifies the specific artifacts and clauses - the chat log, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown - and the facts are corroborated by those artifacts, so the burden is discharged and the point does not defeat the claim. The driver-profile check is clean (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 330 completed trips in 90 days), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No billing-integrity issue arises under POL-RD-09 (nothing charged above the quote, no phantom line, no airport surcharge). The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-04005-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but no party asserts a traffic cause, so it is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The GPS trace is clean under POL-RD-07 (195 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gaps, largest step 216.7 m), so POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered, and no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires - the case does not escalate. Confidence rests on artifacts all at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The monetary effect (SGD 4.80) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold and executes on issue.

To both parties. This was an upfront-quoted trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 22.25, charged_total 22.25, no ERP or toll lines, airport_surcharge 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and the rider owes nothing further and is refunded nothing: charged_total less quoted_fare_sgd is 0.00. The rider's answer — the price was fixed when she booked — is correct as far as her fare is concerned, and her payment state stands unchanged. That is the rider advocate's main point and it is accepted. The driver's SGD 6.00 figure is also not the clause figure: the driver advocate correctly concedes the policy arithmetic. ruling.explanation:
The driver is owed SGD 4.80 (DRIVER_COMPENSATION). The rider's fare does not change.

To the driver: you filed for SGD 6.00 for the extra distance of the Northpoint stop. Your trip was sold as an upfront-quoted fare (quoted and charged SGD 22.25; EV-FARE-04005). On such a trip POL-RD-11 gives the rider no distance-or-time refund, but it says in terms that a rider-requested detour is compensated under POL-RD-04 instead. The rider asked you in-app to stop at Northpoint (MSG-04005-003, sent 15:59:50, before the trip started at 16:00:20) and you agreed four seconds later; the GPS trace passes 55 m from the platform-resolved Northpoint waypoint (EV-GPS-04005), well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test. So the detour was rider-requested and POL-RD-04 applies. Its compensation limb pays SGD 0.75 for every kilometre the rider was billed less than you drove: the fare billed 14.20 km (EV-FARE-04005) while the trace records 20.57 km (EV-GPS-04005), a shortfall of 6.37 km. 6.37 x 0.75 = 4.7775, rounded up to SGD 4.80, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. That is the figure the policy produces; the SGD 6.00 in your filing is not a figure any clause computes, so the ruling moves SGD 4.80, not 6.00.

To the rider: you are right that your fare was fixed at booking and you pay nothing more. The SGD 4.80 is a platform/fee-funded payment to the driver under POL-GEN-03, not a charge on you, so your payment state (CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is left exactly as it is. The amount by which your charge exceeded your quote is SGD 0.00 (charged 22.25 less quoted 22.25), and the fare breakdown carries no ERP, no toll, a 0.00 airport surcharge and a 0.00 waiting-time fee, so there is nothing to correct on your side under POL-RD-11(a) or POL-RD-09. Your point that the driver's filing cites no evidence IDs is rejected: the compensation rests on cited artifacts - the chat log, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown - and POL-RD-08's no-evidence rule does not bar an outcome proved by the bundle.

Why no escalation and no referral: the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (195 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps, largest straight-line step 216.7 m, highest implied speed 78.0 km/h). The POL-RD-06 profile check comes back clean (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 330) and the excess is not material (6.37 km is below the 8.0 km limb and 44.86% below the 50% limb), so no conduct referral arises. The traffic-advisory slot is empty (EV-ADVIS-04005-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), but no party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

Confidence: 0.9. The cap is 1.0 - the deciding facts (the rider instruction and the unbilled kilometre shortfall) rest on EV-CHAT-04005, EV-GPS-04005 and EV-FARE-04005, each at weight_multiplier 1.0. The monetary effect of SGD 4.80 does not exceed the execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it executes automatically unless appealed (POL-GEN-04, POL-GEN-05).

ledger.claim: TRP-04005 was sold and settled as an upfront-quoted trip: the fare breakdown carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 22.25 and distance_charged_km 14.20, and the trip record's booking events fix the quote basis at 14.20 km and 25 minutes. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges on such a trip were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run at all and no fare recomputation is available. The 6.37 km by which the trace exceeds the quote is therefore incapable of being converted into a refund, a recomputed fare, or any rider-side liability - the extra distance is a cost the policy places on the driver on an upfront trip, not a charge the rider can be made to bear.

The rider paid exactly what was quoted and not a cent more: charged_total is 22.25 and quoted_fare_sgd is 22.25, so the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote - the only sum POL-RD-11(a) makes refundable - is 0.00. The fare breakdown shows no ERP lines, no tolls, an airport_surcharge line of 0.00 and a waiting_time_fee of 0.00, so there is no pass-through or statutory line under POL-RD-09 on which any further amount, still less the driver's SGD 6.00, could be built. The present payment state (CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is the complete and correct settlement of this trip, and the driver's claim should be dismissed with that state unchanged.

POL-RD-11 forecloses the very route the driver's claim takes. Its rule states in terms that the driver's unrecovered cost on a detour 'is not recoverable from the rider under this clause', and the SGD 6.00 sought in this dispute is precisely that unrecovered cost. The driver is the filing party; it is for him to point to a clause of the policy in force that shifts his detour cost onto a rider who has already paid the fixed fare in full, and no clause of the route-deviation policy does so. A claim that asks the tribunal to do what the governing clause expressly forbids cannot be granted.

The rider does not dispute that she asked for the stop, and the record fully corroborates her: at 15:59:50 the rider's in-app message asks to stop at Northpoint first, and the platform-resolved waypoint_hint carried on that message sits 55.0 m from the trace's nearest fix - well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test. That concession costs the rider nothing. POL-RD-11 routes a rider-requested detour to POL-RD-04, whose compensation is a policy-rate driver payment, and POL-GEN-03 defines driver_compensation_sgd as a platform-funded or fee-funded payment to the driver - not a charge payable by the rider. Whichever way the causation question is read, the rider's payment state does not change, and no refund or compensation may be levied out of the fixed fare the rider has already paid.

The sum claimed is not produced by any clause's arithmetic. The rider's exposure over the quote is 0.00, and the only distance-based payment the policy provides on these facts is POL-RD-04's rate of SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, capped at SGD 15.00, which on this record's own figures - 20.57 km traced against 14.20 km billed - yields 4.78 rounded up to SGD 4.80. A round figure of SGD 6.00 corresponds to no line of the fare breakdown and to no formula in the policy, and to the extent any such payment were made it is, under POL-GEN-03, a platform-funded or fee-funded payment to the driver rather than a rider charge. The claim as filed cannot be granted in the form pleaded.

The driver's filing identifies no artifact and names no clause: the claim text asserts a detour and demands SGD 6.00, without citing a single evidence ID. POL-RD-08 requires a party invoking an exculpatory or compensatory clause to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and provides that an assertion which cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. The driver is the party asserting that money is owed and so carries the burden of proving the facts that make it owed; an uncited assertion does not discharge that burden, and the artifacts in the bundle that do speak to the request are the rider's own message and the trace, not the driver's pleading.

The chat log carries a rider instruction to make the Northpoint stop: MSG-04005-003, sent by RIDER R-1846 at 2026-09-27T15:59:50, reads 'uncle later can stop at Northpoint first? need to collect my cake, 5 min only then go AMK', and the platform resolved its waypoint_hint at ingest to 1.4289, 103.8357 labelled 'Northpoint City'. The driver accepted four seconds later ('ok can', MSG-04005-004). POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are therefore met: the instruction comes from the rider, not the driver, and it identifies a place specifically enough to act on rather than something vague like 'go the fast way'.

POL-RD-04(b) and the corroboration limb are met on timestamps and coordinates. The instruction was sent at 15:59:50, before the trip started at 16:00:20 and before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, so it is inside the three-minute allowance. The gps_trace corroborates it exactly as the clause requires: the nearest fix to the resolved waypoint_hint (fix index 97, 16:16:26) is 55.0 m away, far inside the 200 m threshold that POL-RD-04 sets, and the derived waypoint_approach block marks within_threshold true.

The rider's own counterparty_statement concedes the request in terms: 'Yes I asked him to stop at Northpoint'. Her only objection is to paying more, not to whether she asked, so the factual foundation of the driver's case - a rider-requested detour actually driven - is common ground on the file and not something the driver has to prove against her.

The deviation the driver complains of is real and measured, not asserted. The governing trace figure under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km 20.57 km against a booked optimal of 14.2 km, an excess of 6.37 km or 44.86%, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). The record shows one off-corridor waypoint, corroborated to within 55 m, and no other instruction in the chat log, so under POL-RD-04 the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied and is not chargeable against the driver.

Separately from the exoneration, and on the face of the ledger, POL-RD-04's compensation limb is satisfied: fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 14.20 while the gps_trace records 20.57 km, so the rider was billed for 6.37 km less than was driven - a shortfall well above the 1.0 km trigger. At the policy's SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre the compensation is 6.37 x 0.75 = SGD 4.7775, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 4.80, and that is inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap.

The rider's answer - 'the price was fixed when I booked' - does not defeat this claim, and the driver does not fight it. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted 22.25, charged_total 22.25, no ERP lines, no surcharge, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so under POL-RD-11 there is no distance-or-time refund for the rider however large the excess; POL-RD-11 expressly says the driver's unrecovered cost on a rider-requested detour is compensated under POL-RD-04 instead. The rider loses nothing and the driver is paid on the clause the policy names.

The policy arithmetic, not the driver's ask, fixes the figure, and the driver accepts it. He filed for SGD 6.00; POL-RD-04 yields SGD 4.80 on 6.37 unbilled kilometres. Under POL-GEN-03 a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling carries amount_sgd at the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd, which is the outcome this record licenses on the merits.

Every artifact this claim rests on is clean, so no escalation or discount is in play. EV-CHAT-04005, EV-TRIP-04005, EV-FARE-04005 and EV-GPS-04005 are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, and the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 195 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, largest interval 10 s, largest straight-line step 216.7 m and highest implied speed 78.0 km/h - nowhere near the 90 s gap, 500 m jump or 30 s cadence limbs. Confidence is therefore not capped below the 0.70 floor under POL-GEN-02(2) and POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered.

The driver-profile check that POL-RD-06 requires comes back clean and should be recorded as such. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 330, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established: no balance is resolved against the driver, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available on this trip and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The excess is in any event not MATERIAL - 6.37 km is under the 8.0 km limb and 44.86% is under the 50% limb.

For completeness and disclosure: no traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-04005-01 is MISSING - admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, payload null - and I name that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. The driver asserts no external traffic cause at all, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked, that absence is not an exculpatory clause invoked against any cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it; the driver's case stands on the chat log and the trace, not on an empty advisory slot.
